user_reviews.Description:
A peaceful Sunday morning coffee escape in Every Half’s lush green courtyard
​Every Half Coffee Roasters offers a beautifully designed, rustic sanctuary that is absolutely perfect for anyone looking to unwind on a relaxing Sunday morning. The standout feature of this location is its expansive, open-air courtyard nestled between sleek navy-blue buildings. Shaded by a canopy of mature, vibrant green trees and filled with climbing plants, the outdoor setup provides an incredibly breezy, refreshing, and visual treat that instantly puts you at ease.
​The Space: The cafe beautifully balances a bright, air-conditioned indoor area with wide panoramic glass walls and a spacious outdoor seating arrangement. The minimalist white and black folding chairs are neatly arranged on patterned stone tiles alongside long wooden benches, creating a variety of casual, comfortable spots to sit back, enjoy the morning sun, and watch the day go by.
​The Coffee: The establishment caters excellently to coffee enthusiasts with a well-curated beverage menu. Their single-origin espresso selection—such as the African blend featuring half Ethiopia Natural and half Ethiopia Washed—is exceptionally well-crafted. It delivers a smooth, balanced flavor profile with delicate floral, chocolate, citrus, and blueberry tasting notes, making it a stellar premium choice for a morning caffeine fix.
​The indoor ordering counter is meticulously organized and clean, displaying their signature drinks, fresh teas, and cold brews alongside friendly service. Whether you prefer to find a quiet corner inside to focus or relax outside under the leafy shade to enjoy the weekend atmosphere, this open-air corner provides a thoroughly delightful and peaceful neighborhood retreat.

user_reviews.Name: Justin Wong
user_reviews.Description:
After hearing the hype around Hoff Coffee Brewers, expectations were naturally set quite high. Unfortunately, it didn’t quite live up to them.

The Iced Salted Caramel Coffee tasted like a watered-down version of what you’d expect from a commercial chain café. The caramel was vague and the advertised saltiness barely came through, resulting in a rather ordinary milky concoction.

The Hoff Beo, their signature drink, was beautifully presented and certainly photogenic. However, it lacked the depth and intensity of the coffee itself. The generous layer of cream became the dominant flavour, masking much of the espresso. It seems to be Hoff’s signature style, but for those looking for coffee-forward drinks, it may feel underwhelming.

The Cà Phê Đen was probably the saving grace. Simple, well chilled and pleasantly robust with toasty notes. It wasn’t particularly complex, but it delivered exactly what an iced black coffee should.

The café itself is tucked away on the second floor through a motorcycle parking area. The interior is clean enough but relatively simple and, compared with some of Ho Chi Minh City’s leading specialty cafés, lacks a distinctive identity or memorable atmosphere.

Verdict

A café with attractive presentation and approachable drinks, but it falls short as a destination specialty coffee experience. After visiting places like XLIII, Lacàph, 96B, Bosgaurus, and even The Workshop, Hoff feels a tier below in both coffee execution and overall experience.

My rating: 3/5

Google rating: 4/5 — the team is clearly putting in effort, and while it wasn’t a standout for me, I’d rather encourage improvement than let one review disproportionately affect a local business.

10/10 would recommend XLIII Coffee, especially if you’re interested in specialty coffee and want someone who genuinely knows and loves what they do!

We highly recommend Little Hanoi to anyone visiting Ho Chi Minh City! ❤️🙏🏻🍵☕️

If you love coffee, GET HERE. Bosgaurus isn't just a café — it's an experience. Absolutely stellar. ☕✨

Soo Kafe Bến Thành is one of those hidden gems that feels like you’ve stumbled into a secret world. Tucked away in a small, dimly lit alley, the journey to the café already sets a mysterious mood before you even step inside.

The interior reminds me of an old bookstore combined with a cozy comic book library. Shelves filled with books, warm lighting, and the quiet atmosphere make it the perfect place to escape the busy streets outside. Despite its small size, every corner feels thoughtfully designed and incredibly inviting.

The drink menu is surprisingly extensive, offering plenty of choices whether you’re into specialty coffee, tea, or creative signature beverages. It’s easy to spend hours here reading, chatting with friends, or simply enjoying the peaceful ambiance.

If you’re looking for a café with character rather than just another Instagram spot, Soo Kafe Bến Thành is definitely worth a visit. The unique atmosphere alone makes it memorable, and the wide selection of drinks is the icing on the cake.

The Workshop is one of Ho Chi Minh City’s most well-known specialty coffee shops, tucked away in an old building on Ngo Duc Ke Street. Finding the entrance can be a little confusing the first time, but once you’re inside, you’re greeted by a spacious industrial-style café with high ceilings, large windows, and a relaxing atmosphere.

The coffee is clearly the highlight here. They offer a wide selection of beans and brewing methods, and the baristas are knowledgeable and passionate about what they do. I tried a pour-over, and it was smooth, aromatic, and full of flavor. It’s definitely a great place for anyone who appreciates high-quality coffee.

The café has a calm and stylish vibe, although it’s more of a destination for enjoying a carefully crafted cup than a place to spend the whole day working. If you’re a coffee lover visiting Ho Chi Minh City, The Workshop is absolutely worth experiencing at least once.
